body: FWIW rc2 is now out
PR here: https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml/pull/963
Any update on this? Official 3.15 should be live this week.
Looks like the wheels are now being correctly built (since #971), but they are not yet being uploaded to PyPI.
Any idea when upload to PyPI can be expected?

> 15\. Any idea when upload to PyPI can be expected?

YAMLRocks seems to support Python 3.15 already (and also claims to be much faster than PyYAML while remaining compatible): https://github.com/frenck/YAMLRocks/releases#release-v0.7.0
an issue tracker is no place to advertise slopware. Pyyaml is a crucial dependencies to a large ecosystem and cannot (and should not) be swapped out for an alternative overnight.

Until the 3.15 wheels are on PyPI, a workaround that worked for me on Windows 11 without any compiler: build PyYAML without the C extension.
```powershell
$env:PYYAML_FORCE_LIBYAML = "0"
pip install pyyaml
```
On Python 3.15.0 this installed 6.0.3 as pure Python (`yaml.__with_libyaml__` is `False`), and packages that depend on it, like transformers 5.19.0, then installed normally. Without it, pip tries to compile and fails with "Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or greater is required". Slower YAML parsing, but it unblocks 3.15 testing. Write-up with the other 3.15 failures: https://nilaykabariya.blog/tested/python-3-15-windows-packages-tested
@nitzmahone, thanks for merging https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml/pull/971. Any idea when 3.15 will show up on PyPI? Anything you need help with to get it there?

Data point on 3.15.0 final (released Oct 9): PyYAML 6.0.3 builds from the sdist and works fine in our `ultralytics` predict/train/val smoke tests on macOS arm64, but only as pure Python (`yaml.__with_libyaml__ == False`). Wheel publication is now requested in #981.

Another data point for 3.15.0 wheels: Camoufox imports `yaml.CLoader` directly, so on 3.15 it fails at import with `cannot import name 'CLoader'` unless PyYAML is compiled from source against libyaml. That means a C toolchain on every user's machine. We've pinned our installs to 3.14 for now. Since #971 is merged, is a 6.0.4 release with cp315 wheels possible? Happy to help test.
While waiting for pypi, the wheels can be installed from https://github.com/yaml/pyyaml/actions/runs/37695338325/artifacts/11514809890
If the release has been tagged, do we know what is blocking the PyPI upload?
Any News here?

One potentially relevant detail: PyPI [announced in July that it rejects new files uploaded to releases more than 14 days old](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/), including wheels adding support for newer Python versions.

Since 6.0.3 predates that window, publishing the Python 3.15 wheels would appear to require a new release rather than adding them to 6.0.3.

I haven’t seen confirmation that this is the blocker here, but wanted to surface the policy in case it helps clarify the publication path.
@nitzmahone This is urgent
It is not. Could we as a community refrain from harassing maintainers and release managers once a year when a new Python version drops ?

Adventurous users can try https://yaml.rocks/, which supports 3.15, is faster, has more features, including a PyYAML compatibility mode. Times like these are an opportunity to revisit one's dependencies. Best of luck to the maintainers.

For anyone who needs PyYAML on 3.15 before the wheels are on PyPI: on Windows without the MSVC build tools, you can skip the C extension and build the pure-Python version:

```powershell
$env:PYYAML_FORCE_LIBYAML = "0"
pip install pyyaml
```

On Python 3.15.2 with no compiler, that installed 6.0.3 and `import yaml` worked. A `pyyaml==6.0.1` pin installed the same way. The catch is the one mentioned above: a pure build has no libyaml, so code that imports `CLoader` or `CSafeLoader` still needs a compiled build (or 3.14).

On Linux, `python:3.15-slim` falls back to the pure build without printing any error, and `yaml.__with_libyaml__` is `False`. If you move a slim image to 3.15, check that flag.

Reproduction and runs: https://nilaykabariya.blog/fixes/failed-building-wheel-for-pyyaml

Can we get an official status update? 
Also; it is weird to ask why these Python version specific wheels are nececary and this library cannot use an "any" wheel like most libraries do?

@Houbein `any` wheels are for pure-python. You probably mean `abi3` but they are usually difficult to get right and require great care to build and test. I'm working to have a few of my projects support this, and it's somewhat challenging, depending on the internals. It limits what a project can use internally. For example, per-version wheels can get away with "private" C-API use but wheels you want have to be compiled against the limited API of CPython, meaning that certain things aren't allowed to be used. When using pure C, it's difficult to instrument. Transpilers like Cython simplify producing such wheels (with similar limitations) by hiding some internals but at a cost of losing the ability to measure code coverage, for example.

In general, it's a lot of initial work. But if you get a wheel tagged `py36-abi3`, it's supposed to work with Python 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 etc. (theoretically)

But again, volunteer-led projects mean that people end up having to prioritize where their effort is best spent. If you see the maintainers at meetups and conferences, say hi and thank them.
